title: The two F D A pharmacogenomic tables

segs.text: Section twenty three. The two F D A tables. The F D A keeps two online tables of drugs with a known gene drug link, and they answer different questions. The first is the Table of Pharmacogenetic Associations: drugs for which the F D A believes there is sufficient evidence that certain genetic variants alter drug metabolism, therapeutic effect, or the risk of adverse events. Being listed does not necessarily mean the F D A advocates a pharmacogenetic test before prescribing, unless the test is a companion diagnostic.

It has three sections, by strength of data. Section one: the data support therapeutic management recommendations; she called it the most substantial. Section two: the data indicate a potential impact on safety or response. Section three: the data show a potential impact on pharmacokinetic properties only, the lightest. So section one is the strongest, not section three.

Its application is initial screening for drugs with pharmacogenetic implications. Its limitation is that it lacks detailed guidance on clinical application: it names the drug, gene and affected group, but not what to do for a patient.

The second table, the one she prefers, is the Table of Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers in Drug Labeling. It lists every F D A approved drug whose label contains pharmacogenomic information. That includes germline or somatic gene variants, functional deficiencies, gene expression variations, chromosomal abnormalities, and protein biomarkers used to select therapy. It leaves out non human genetic biomarkers, biomarkers used only for diagnosis, and biomarkers related to a drug other than the referenced drug.

Why only the referenced drug? Label information comes from data on that drug. The S L C O one B one transporter data were for simvastatin, so the table speaks only about simvastatin; we cannot assume another statin responds the same way to that biomarker.

For each drug, this table also names the sections of the label that discuss pharmacogenomics. For abacavir: Boxed Warning, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, and Warnings and Precautions. Every F D A label uses the same sections, so a pharmacist checking for a pharmacogenomic boxed warning or genotype based dosing goes straight to the section named. Its application is helping pharmacists make informed decisions on medication therapy management from the latest labeling. Its limitation is scope and lag: only F D A approved drugs, and it may miss emerging information, because it follows the labels and is updated periodically.
